questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The induced electromotive force between the ends of the rod is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf in a rotating rod of length $l$ about one end is:
$e = \int_0^l v B \, \mathrm{d}r = \int_0^l (\omega r) B \, \mathrm{d}r = B \omega \left[ \frac{r^2}{2} \right]_0^l = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The induced electromotive force (emf) between the two ends of the rod is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf $e$ in a rotating rod is given by integrating $de = B v dx = B (\omega x) dx$ from $0$ to $l$.
$e = \int_0^l B \omega x dx = B \omega \left[ \frac{x^2}{2} \right]_0^l = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $L$ is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ about one of its ends in a uniform magnetic field $B$ acting perpendicular to the plane of rotation. The induced electromotive force (emf) between the two ends of the rod is:
questions.solution: Induced emf for a rotating rod is $e = \int_0^L B v \, dr = \int_0^L B (r\omega) \, dr = B\omega \left[\frac{r^2}{2}\right]_0^L = \frac{1}{2} B L^2 \omega$.

questions.stem: A metallic rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular speed $\omega$ about an axis passing through one end and perpendicular to its length, in a uniform magnetic field $B$ parallel to the axis of rotation. The induced emf between the ends of the rod is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf is given by integrating $de = B v dr = B (\omega r) dr$ from $0$ to $l$.
$e = B \omega \int_{0}^{l} r dr = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.stem: A metallic rod of length $1 \mathrm{m}$ is rotated with a frequency of $10 \mathrm{Hz}$ about an axis passing through its one end and perpendicular to its length, in a uniform magnetic field of $0.1 \mathrm{T}$ directed perpendicular to the plane of rotation. The induced emf between the ends of the rod is $\frac{\pi}{x} \mathrm{V}$. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf in a rotating rod is given by $\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega L^2$.
Here, $L = 1 \mathrm{m}$, $B = 0.1 \mathrm{T}$, and $f = 10 \mathrm{Hz} \implies \omega = 2\pi f = 20\pi \mathrm{rad/s}$.
$\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.1 \times 20\pi \times 1^2 = \pi \mathrm{V}$.
Comparing with $\frac{\pi}{x}$, we get $x = 1$.

questions.stem: A metal rod of length $l$ rotates with an angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis perpendicular to its length and passing through one of its ends, in a uniform magnetic field $B$ parallel to the axis. The induced electromotive force between the two ends of the rod is:
questions.solution: The induced emf for a rotating rod is given by $e = \int_0^l B v \, dx = \int_0^l B (\omega x) \, dx = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.stem: A metallic rod of length $1\ \mathrm{m}$ is rotated with a frequency of $50\ \mathrm{rev/s}$ with one end hinged at the center and the other end at the circumference of a circular metallic ring of radius $1\ \mathrm{m}$, about an axis passing through the center and perpendicular to the plane of the ring. A constant and uniform magnetic field of $2\ \mathrm{T}$ parallel to the axis is present everywhere. The emf induced between the center and the metallic ring is _________ $\mathrm{V}$.
questions.solution:
Induced emf in a rotating rod is $e = \frac{1}{2} B \omega L^2$.
Here $B = 2\ \mathrm{T}$, $L = 1\ \mathrm{m}$, and $\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi (50) = 100\pi\ \mathrm{rad/s}$.
$e = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 100\pi \times 1^2 = 100\pi\ \mathrm{V} \approx 100 \times 3.1416 = 314\ \mathrm{V}$.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The induced emf between the ends of the rod is:
questions.solution:
The induced motional emf in a rotating rod is obtained by integrating $de = B v dr = B (\omega r) dr$ from $0$ to $l$:
$e = \int_0^l B \omega r dr = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $1\ \mathrm{m}$ is rotated with a constant angular speed of $10\ \mathrm{rad/s}$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of $0.4\ \mathrm{T}$. The induced potential difference (in $\mathrm{V}$) between the two ends of the rod is ______.
questions.solution:
The induced emf between the ends of a rotating rod is given by $e = \frac{1}{2} B \omega L^2$.
Given $B = 0.4\ \mathrm{T}$, $\omega = 10\ \mathrm{rad/s}$, and $L = 1\ \mathrm{m}$.
$e = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.4 \times 10 \times 1^2 = 2\ \mathrm{V}$.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular speed $\omega$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The induced emf between the two ends of the rod is:

$e = \int_0^l (v B) dr = \int_0^l (\omega r B) dr = B \omega \left[ \frac{r^2}{2} \right]_0^l = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.solution: The induced emf in a rotating rod is given by $\varepsilon = \int_0^L B v \, dx = \int_0^L B (\omega x) \, dx = B \omega \left[ \frac{x^2}{2} \right]_0^L = \frac{1}{2} B \omega L^2$.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The induced emf between the two ends of the rod is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf in a rotating rod of length $l$ about one end is given by:
$e = \int_0^l B v \, dx = \int_0^l B (\omega x) \, dx = B \omega \left[ \frac{x^2}{2} \right]_0^l = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.stem: A conducting square loop of side length $l$ and resistance $R$ moves in its plane with a uniform velocity $v$ perpendicular to one of its sides. A magnetic field $B$, constant in time and space, pointing perpendicular to the plane of the loop, exists everywhere. The current induced in the loop is:
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux $\Phi = B A$ through the loop remains constant as it moves through a completely uniform magnetic field. 
Thus, $\frac{d\Phi}{dt} = 0$, and the induced electromotive force (and hence the induced current) is zero.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $1\ \mathrm{m}$ is rotated with a constant angular speed of $4\ \mathrm{rad/s}$ about an axis passing through one of its ends and perpendicular to its length, in a uniform magnetic field of $0.5\ \mathrm{T}$ directed parallel to the axis of rotation. The induced emf between the two ends of the rod is _________ $\mathrm{V}$.
questions.solution:
The induced emf in a rotating rod is given by $\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega L^2$.
Substitute $B = 0.5\ \mathrm{T}$, $\omega = 4\ \mathrm{rad/s}$, and $L = 1\ \mathrm{m}$:
$\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.5 \times 4 \times 1^2 = 1\ \mathrm{V}$.

questions.stem: A conducting square loop of side $L$ and resistance $R$ moves in its plane with a uniform velocity $v$ perpendicular to one of its sides. A magnetic field $B$, constant in time and space, pointing perpendicular to the plane of the loop exists everywhere. The current induced in the loop is:
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux through the loop is $\Phi = B A = B L^2 = \text{constant}$.
Since flux does not change with time, the induced emf $\varepsilon = -\frac{d\Phi}{dt} = 0$.
Therefore, the induced current is zero.

questions.stem: A metal rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ about an axis passing through one of its ends and perpendicular to its length, in a uniform magnetic field $B$ directed parallel to the axis of rotation. The induced EMF between the two ends of the rod is:
questions.solution:
The induced EMF in a small element $dx$ at distance $x$ from the pivot is $d\varepsilon = B v dx = B (\omega x) dx$.
Integrating from $0$ to $l$:
$\varepsilon = \int_0^l B \omega x dx = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.
